newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Dec 24.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Dec 24.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Former Wallabies rugby union captain Phil Kearns, who missed all of the 1996 representative season through an injury to his Achilles tendon, should return to the game in February. Kearns, who is Australia's most capped hooker, came through a workout atteded by five New South Wales internationals all on the comeback trail after injury. Page 16.

Swimming coach Scott Volkers, who coached Susie O'Neill to her gold medal swim at the Atlanta Olympics, is using innovative paddles to develop 15-year-old Kristy Ellem into his latest world No. 1 ranked swimmer. While only working with Volkers for eight months, Ellem has already developed a stroke similar to Volkers' breastroker Samantha Riley. Page 16.

FIFA general secretary Sepp Blatter, one of the most influential figures in world soccer, believes that if Sydney can host the 2000 Olympics successfully, it should make a bid to run the soccer World Cup in 2006, the world's second biggest sporting event. Page 16.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australia's cricket selectors have discarded their past policy of loyalty by dropping batsman Ricky Ponting and bowler Michael Kasprowicz for newcomers Justin Langer and Matthew Hayden for the selection of the Australian team to play in the Boxing day Test against the West Indies. Page 34.

Sydney to Hobart yacht race favourite Morning Glory has already suffered a set back to its quest to win the 630-nautical-mile classic when it broke the top six metres off its 33.5 metre carbon-fibre mast during a training sail off Sydney Heads on Saturday and the crew are now waiting for a spare mast to be flown in from Auckland and installed. Page 34.

Following the axing of three of its teams for the 1997 season, the National Basketball League announced yesterday some games for the 1997 season were to be scheduled in New Zealand and western Sydney. Reigning champions South East Melbourne Magic will play the Illawarra Hawks in Liverpool in May, and in September will play the Newcastle Falcons in Christchurch. Page 33.
THE AGE

As the Australian cricket selectors announced the team for the Boxing Day Test against the West Indies in Melbourne, the West Indies are considering using wicketkeeper Junior Murray, who hit an impressive 86 against Pakistan in the one-day match in Adelaide, as opening batsman, says manager Clive Lloyd. Page C8.

Victorian Jockeys' Association president Neville Wilson said that a national telephone hook-up of State jockey's union executives decided that if their bid of an increased riding fee is not met by Christmas Day, industrial action would begin. Page C8.

The 0-0 draw between the Collingwood Warriors and UTS Olympic in the Ericsson Cup match at Victoria Park last night was as dreary a game as one could see, with most players' performances sluggish after both teams suffered large defeats two nights earlier. Page C8.
THE HERALD SUN

New South Wales cricketer Michael Bevan will join Ricky Ponting as another victim of the Australian cricket selectors' daring "first comes first" philosophy as his place in the Test team will only see him dropped to 12th man, despite a last start Test 50 nd an improved rating as a slow bowler. Page 72.

West Australian batsman Justin Langer was all smiles after being named in the Australian cricket Test side to play against the West Indies on Boxing Day. Langer ensured his position by piling up scores of 143 not out, 116 and 274 not out in his past three Sheffield Shield matches. Page 68.

The national under 20 men's waterpolo championships will be held in Sydney from January 5-11, and the Victorian team members have been told to lay off the Christmas celebration drinks as they face hard training for the event. Coach Daniel Flahive said the team had finished fourth in the past two championships, yet this year has a good chance of a medal. Page 64.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Sydney Swans AFL player Tony Lockett could face a jail term after being charged with 27 counts relating to alleged irregularities in the greyhound breeding work of his star stud dog Malawi's Prince. The charges include eight counts of obtaining property by deception, nine each of making and using a false document, and one of obtaining financial advantage by deception. Page 60.

South Australian bowler Jason Gillespie was an unlikely hero with the bat in yesterday's Sheffield Shield cricket match between South Australia and Western Australia at the WACA Ground in Perth. Gillespie stayed on the crease for 268 minutes, faced 227 blls, and hit a career-best score of 58. Page 55.

The Western Suburbs rugby league side has signed two Fijians and two Tongans to its side for the 1997 season. Coach Tom Raudonikis said the players were spotted playing New South Wales Country rugby league and the team has high hopes for the quartet in the lead up to the 1997 season. Page 53.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
